pr_title: Cygwin: Restore support for old versions (without `dladdr` and `Dl_info`).
pr_body:
But if a new enough version of Cygwin is detected,
we continue to take advantage of the presence of `dladdr` and `Dl_info`
(as per #9402 i.e. commit 38f6f99c).

"Detection" is based on diff's introduced in Cygwin on 2017-03-08
(`CYGWIN_VERSION_API_MINOR` bumped to `308` upon introduction of `dladdr`):
<https://cygwin.com/git/?p=newlib-cygwin.git;a=commit;h=c8432a01c8401c121940c806a9d868c4adc4cefd>.

Fixes #10200.

I was unaware of the dependence to the perl version. Upgrading perl solves the problem (at least for me) and 1.1.1d builds fine.
```
    /usr/bin/perl
    5.26.3 for i686-cygwin-threads-64int-multi
````
There should be some check in place to clear that up while configuring?

This issue has nothing to do with perl versions, and everything to do with the availability of Dl_info and dladdr(), which we require since #9402.  That's why you needed to update Cygwin to be able to build.

If anyone wants to submit a PR that detects the presence of Dl_info, it's welcome.
#9402 has been merged since I last commented, so this issue is now fixed.

review_comments: I am not sure this lengthy commentary can be really regarded as something to be committed with CLA: trivial. Also IMO it does not belong here - I'd put it into the commit message and here just add one or two sentences.

I believe that the evil practices of Cygwin -- forcing new versions of Windows upon us -- should be exposed visibly, in a comment in the source code. That is also going to prevent someone else from breaking support for older versions in the future.

Regarding the CLA: It is not like I am going to sue any organization because it has used my (possibly un-welcome anyway) lengthy comments (or that such a suing action would have success). This change is trivial -- one line of code (within a pre-processor directive, too).

The comments are meant to clarify the history of the situation. They can easily be ignored by Humans as they are ignored by the Compiler.

But the comments might help a Human who is interested in those lines of code -- to quickly get a picture of the situation without checking the Git log or the comments on the Github Pull Request webpage -- especially since Github itself might disappear -- just like support for old versions of Windows and Cygwin is disappearing -- Time beats us all. :'(

Is it possible to remove the "Requires CLA" mark, please ? (-:
